title: Use sub-millisecond timestamps in LLM event logs so they have a natural deterministic order
description:
Golden export tests currently sort llmEvents and llmTrace by their full JSON content because events from different players can interleave with identical or sub-millisecond timestamp differences. After stripping timestamps for comparison, the sort order is fragile.

If the logs themselves had sub-millisecond (e.g. microsecond or nanosecond) timestamps, or monotonic sequence numbers, the events would have a natural deterministic order and golden tests wouldn't need to sort by content.

The timestamps are written by the puppeteer's LLM event logging. Adding a monotonic sequence counter or using time.time_ns() / time.perf_counter_ns() instead of time.time() would give each event a unique, deterministic ordering.

Revalidated on 2026-02-22: still relevant. `GameLogWriter.emit` currently uses millisecond timestamps (`datetime.now(...).isoformat(timespec="milliseconds")`), and export golden normalization still sorts LLM events by content after stripping `ts`.
